samples.summary: `inheritable` gate narrows the spec'd unset rule, so non-plain/number formats keep residue. The todo (docs/tasks/active/20260818-sheets-decimal-round-trip-todo.md:50-53) specifies: `target === valueDp` and `explicitDp` → try to unset, using `['dp','nf']` when `nf === 'number'` and **`['dp']` otherwise**. The implementation instead only attempts an unset when `!nf || nf === 'plain' || nf === 'number'`, so a `currency`/`percent`/date-formatted cell with an explicit `dp` never returns to inheritance: e.g. currency cell holding `12.34` (valueDp 2, default dp 2) → Increase writes `dp: 3` → Decrease targets 2 === valueDp but is blocked by `inheritable`, storing `dp: 2` residue instead of unsetting. That is the same residue class the issue's outcome ("leave a cell exactly as it started") is about, just for a different number format.

samples.summary: Plan/implementation placement mismatch left unreconciled: the todo item 3 (checked as done) specifies a private `Spreadsheet.applyDecimalDelta(delta)` that both handlers collapse onto; the branch instead adds public `Sheet.changeDecimals(delta)` in the model layer and the view handlers delegate. The model placement is arguably the better layer (it sits beside `setRangeStyle`/`toggleRangeStyle`), but the plan doc was ticked off without being updated, so the recorded spec no longer describes the code.

Removing `dp: 2` from `DefaultStyleValues` is unrequested scope with cross-feature reach: it changes `pruneRedundantDefaultStyleKeys` for every `dp` write in the product (toolbar number formats, xlsx import, autofill, range-patch compaction/merging), not just the decimal buttons — patches that previously self-erased or merged away now persist. It is justified in the doc/comment and is arguably needed for `explicitDp`, but it is a storage-semantics change to shared machinery that no todo task item asked for, and `DefaultResetStylePatch` (sheet.ts:144) still has no `dp`, so "clear formatting" now leaves a stored `dp` behind.

`removeCellStyleKeysInRange` duplicates the existing `clearCellStylesInRange` (sheet.ts:1990) almost line for line — same grid walk, same visited-anchor set, same `compactCell`/`isEmptyCell`/delete-or-set tail. The existing method is the all-keys case of the new one; folding one into the other (or extracting the grid walk) would avoid a third near-identical copy alongside `applyStylePatchToExistingCells`.

verdict.reason: The claimed code is present verbatim at packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:4202-4203 (`const inheritable = !nf || nf === 'plain' || nf === 'number'; if (explicitDp && target === valueDp && inheritable)`). Both spec artifacts state the unnarrowed rule: the todo (docs/tasks/active/20260818-sheets-decimal-round-trip-todo.md:49-53) says unset with `['dp','nf']` when nf === 'number' and `['dp']` otherwise, and the design doc (docs/design/sheets/sheet-style.md:209-213) repeats the rule with no format restriction. The reviewer's trace checks out: a currency cell with no stored dp returns dp:2/explicitDp:false (sheet.ts:4185); Increase writes dp:3 without touching nf (sheet.ts:4213-4217); Decrease hits target === valueDp but is blocked by `inheritable`, storing `dp: 2` residue on a cell that started with none — contradicting the stated outcome "leave a cell exactly as it started ... including leaving no dp/nf behind on a cell that had none". The residue is not always invisible either: formatValue uses the locale default currency fraction digits when dp is undefined (format.ts:135-146; KRW renders 0 decimals per format.test.ts:44-51). No guard elsewhere makes this unreachable, no test covers currency/percent (decimals.test.ts has none), and the lessons log only justifies dropping nf for `nf: 'number'` (lessons.md:19-36), not the exclusion of currency/percent/date. There is a plausible rationale for the narrowing (unsetting dp on percent/currency would fall back to a 2-decimal default), but that argues the spec/doc should be amended, not that the finding is absent, guarded, or out of this lens's lane — spec-conformance against a named acceptance criterion is precisely this reviewer's lane and is major by kind.
